production.note: US model years 2002-2006. Jeff Zurschmeide, Sports Car Market: 'The new Mini entered the market in the 2002' and 'The supercharged R53 was built through the 2006 model year'. MINI USA's press kit: the Cooper S 'went on sale in the U.S. from March 22, 2002' (mini-usa-cooper-s-press-kit-2002). The convertible Cooper S is the separate R52 chassis and is not included.

configuration.note: 'The car is powered by a fourcylinder, 163 horsepower engine'; '1.6-liter transverse-mounted engine'.

aspiration.note: 'The supercharger compresses the fresh air drawn in by the engine to an overpressure of 0.8 bar.'

drivetrain.note: 'Traction Control ensures that the extra power to the front wheels is conveyed safely to the road at all times.' (transverse engine, front-wheel drive)

transmission.note: Manual: 'Transmission type 6-Speed Manual', 'Getrag 285' (mini-usa-cooper-s-press-kit-2002; the 2002 kit lists only the manual). Automatic: Zurschmeide, describing the 2005 update: 'Mini also added an available paddle-shifted 6-speed automatic transmission.'

powerHp.note: Quote (MINI USA press kit, technical data): "Nominal power / engine speed hp 163/ 6000"; text: "At 6,000 rpm, the compact 1.6-liter transverse-mounted engine develops a maximum output of 163 horsepower." 2002 model year (launch). From 2005 the Cooper S was rated 168 hp: Zurschmeide, 'Output got a boost to 168 hp and 161 lb-ft in 2005 with a new Teflon-coated supercharger' (sportscarmarket-r53); Khatir Soltani, Auto123 2005 road test: '168-h.p.' (auto123-cooper-s-2005). 163 hp covers 2002-2004, three of the five model years, so the launch year is the reference year.

weightLb.note: PROVISIONAL (two databases, backed by MINI's own table). 2002 Cooper S, 6-speed manual. Quote (KBB 2002): "Curb Weight | 2315 pounds | 2513 pounds" (Cooper / Cooper S). Conceptcarz: "2513 lbs | 1139.878 kg". MINI USA's press kit gives "Gross vehicle weight / payload lbs 3461 / 948", and 3,461 - 948 = 2,513 lb, but a figure worked out by subtraction cannot carry the record. The kit's "Unladen weight lbs 2678" is 165 lb (75 kg) more: the EU unladen weight including a 75 kg driver, not a curb weight (see discrepancies).

sources.title: MINI Cooper S press kit (2002 US launch)
2005 MINI Cooper S Road Test (Khatir Soltani)
2002 MINI Cooper Specs, Features & Options (Cooper S Hatchback 2D)

discrepancies.reason: MINI USA prints "Unladen weight lbs 2678"; KBB and Conceptcarz give 2,513 lb, which equals MINI's own gross vehicle weight minus payload (3,461 - 948). The 165 lb (75 kg) gap is the EU driver allowance.
discrepancies.resolution: 2,513 lb used: 2,678 lb includes a 75 kg driver, so it is not a curb weight. No manufacturer page states 2,513 lb directly, so the weight is provisional.

discrepancies.reason: Sports Car Market says the original Cooper S "offered 161 horsepower".
discrepancies.resolution: MINI USA's 163 hp used: the manufacturer's rating ranks above an article.

provisionalNote: Weight (2,513 lb) rests on two databases (KBB, Conceptcarz), backed by MINI's own gross-weight-minus-payload arithmetic. A MINI/BMW curb or DIN weight (about 1,140 kg) or a major magazine spec panel would replace it. Power is from MINI USA.
